description: This line plot, from the paper “Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine Translation,” illustrates the relationship between Average Lagging (AL) on the x-axis and BLEU score on the y-axis for four different training strategies, evaluated on the WMT15 German-to-English dataset. The x-axis, labeled “Average Lagging (AL),” spans from 0.0 to 10.0 with tick marks at intervals of 2.5, representing the average delay in token generation during simultaneous translation. The y-axis, labeled “BLEU,” ranges from 18 to 29, with major gridlines every 2 units, indicating the quality of translation output. Four distinct lines are plotted: “Consistency-CE” (purple circles with dotted line) starts at approximately BLEU 18.8 at AL=0.0 and rises to about 27.0 at AL=10.0; “Inconsistency-CE” (purple squares with dashed line) begins near BLEU 20.0 at AL=0.0 and increases to roughly 27.0 at AL=10.0; “Inconsistency-CE-MP” (blue squares with dash-dot line) starts at BLEU 18.5 at AL=0.0 and climbs to about 27.2 at AL=10.0; and “Consistency-Bi” (red stars with solid line) begins at BLEU 22.2 at AL=0.0, rises steeply to BLEU 26.2 at AL=3.75, peaks at BLEU 28.8 at AL=8.75, and slightly declines to BLEU 28.5 at AL=10.0. All lines show an overall upward trend, with “Consistency-Bi” achieving the highest BLEU scores across most AL values.
